column3: cause
column4: remedy   (single source for click_run.sh failure output and docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md)

column3: Unknown flag, stage name or profile.
column4: Run `./run.sh --help`; stages are: preflight venv torch build download verify-model retire-cache serve smoke.

column3: A stage receipt in .state/ is unreadable or the state directory is not writable.
column4: Delete the broken receipt (`rm .state/<stage>.json`) or the whole `.state/` directory; the stage simply runs again.

column3: The machine is not aarch64. This runtime (build flags, pinned torch wheel) is for the GB10 / DGX Spark.
column4: Run on a DGX Spark / GB10. On x86-64 use the upstream ExLlamaV3 wheels with the same pack.

column3: nvidia-smi is missing or reports no GPU.
column4: Install the NVIDIA driver: `sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-580-open && sudo reboot`, then check `nvidia-smi`.

column3: The NVIDIA driver is older than 580, which is the first branch that supports CUDA 13.
column4: `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y --only-upgrade nvidia-driver-580-open && sudo reboot`.

column3: No GPU with compute capability 12.1 (SM121, GB10).
column4: Use a GB10 / DGX Spark. Other GPUs need a different TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST and are untested.

column3: Another process is already computing on the GPU; on GB10 it shares the same 128 GB pool.
column4: Stop it (`nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps=pid,process_name --format=csv`), or re-run with `--allow-busy` at your own risk.

column3: git, gcc, g++ or curl is missing.
column4: `sudo apt-get install -y build-essential git curl`.

column3: No Python 3.11 to 3.13 found.
column4: `sudo apt-get install -y python3.12 python3.12-venv`, or `PYTHON=/path/to/python3.12 ./run.sh`.

column3: `python -m venv` failed (usually the venv/ensurepip package is missing).
column4: `sudo apt-get install -y python3.12-venv` (match your Python), then re-run.

column3: nvcc 13.x was not found; it is needed once to compile the ExLlamaV3 CUDA extension.
column4: `sudo apt-get install -y cuda-toolkit-13-0 && export CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.0`, or reuse a cached wheel (`CACHE_DIR=...`).

column3: Not enough free disk for the model (26.4 GiB), the venv (about 14 GiB) and the build.
column4: Free space, or point MODEL_DIR / VENV / CACHE_DIR at a larger disk.

column3: MemAvailable is below what the profile needs (see docs/MEMORY.md).
column4: Stop other memory users, or choose a smaller profile: `./run.sh --profile gb10-text-32k` / `gb10-text-16k-lowmem`.

column3: The listen port is already in use.
column4: `PORT=8001 ./run.sh`, or find the owner: `ss -ltnp | grep :8000`.

column3: pip could not install the pinned torch wheel from the PyTorch index.
column4: Check network/proxy access to download.pytorch.org and re-run; the stage resumes.

column3: pip could not install the pinned runtime requirements.
column4: Check network access to pypi.org; read the pip error in `.state/logs/torch.log`; re-run.

column3: Fetching the pinned ExLlamaV3 commit from GitHub failed.
column4: Check network/proxy access to github.com; the fetch is resumable, re-run.

column3: The fetched ExLlamaV3 tree is not the commit pinned in runtime.lock.json.
column4: Delete `$CACHE_DIR/src/exllamav3-*` and re-run; if it persists the pin is unreachable, open an issue.

column3: Compiling the ExLlamaV3 CUDA extension failed.
column4: Read the tail printed above (full log `.state/logs/build.log`). Typical causes: wrong nvcc (need 13.x), out of memory (`BUILD_JOBS=4 ./run.sh`), missing g++.

column3: The built extension does not import, or the MiniCPM-V-4.7 architecture is not registered.
column4: `./run.sh --force --only build` rebuilds; make sure the venv torch matches runtime.lock.json.

column3: `hf download` failed (network, disk, or Hugging Face rate limit).
column4: Re-run: downloads resume. On HTTP 429 wait a few minutes; lower `DL_WORKERS=2`; anonymous access is enough, no token is needed.

column3: The model directory is not the pinned revision and no UPLOAD_MANIFEST.json is present to verify against.
column4: Use the pinned pack (default), or put the repo's UPLOAD_MANIFEST.json next to the shards, or `SKIP_VERIFY=1` to accept the risk.

column3: A shard or metadata file differs in size or sha256 from the pinned manifest.
column4: `./run.sh --force --only download` then `--only verify-model --verify-model`. If it persists, the files on disk are damaged.

column3: Shard page cache could not be retired, or physical MemFree is below the model + workspace budget.
column4: Close other large processes and re-run `./run.sh --from retire-cache`; see docs/MEMORY.md (page cache on unified memory).

column3: `Insufficient VRAM in split for model and cache`: the loader saw too little free memory, normally because shard page cache counted as used.
column4: `./run.sh --from retire-cache` (retires only the shard pages), make sure nothing else uses the GPU, or pick a smaller profile.

column3: The server process exited before it was ready.
column4: Read the log tail printed above (`.state/logs/serve.log`) and `scripts/env_report.sh` output.

column3: The server did not become ready within READY_TIMEOUT seconds.
column4: Look at `.state/logs/serve.log`; a cold load of the 26 GiB pack can take minutes on slow disks: `READY_TIMEOUT=3600 ./run.sh`.

column3: A smoke request failed (HTTP error, wrong answer, or malformed response).
column4: Read the failing check above; the server stays up for inspection: `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8000/health`.

column3: The optional memory guard (GUARD=1) could not start.
column4: Unset GUARD or read `.state/logs/guard.log`.
